dublinCore.description: Designs low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-stop, notch, comb and all-pass filters at fs = 8000 Hz as an IIR biquad cascade, an IIR direct form or an FIR filter, and shows the magnitude response with the ideal brick-wall response, the phase, group delay, impulse and step responses, the pole-zero plot with a stability indicator, the effect of rounding the coefficients to B bits, and what the filter does to a test signal made of 200, 1000 and 3000 Hz tones.

learningObjectives: Classify low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-stop, notch, comb and all-pass filters by which of the 200, 1000 and 3000 Hz test tones each one passes or removes
Explain why raising the order of a Butterworth filter steepens the transition band without moving the -3 dB frequency
Compare FIR and IIR designs using their pole locations, group delay and impulse responses
Calculate the peak and dip frequencies of a comb filter from fs/D and choose D to remove given tones
Analyze how rounding the coefficients moves poles, and why a biquad cascade survives rounding that makes the same filter unstable in direct form
prerequisites: Poles, zeros and the unit circle
Frequency response in decibels and phase

misconceptions.misconception: A higher-order filter has a lower cutoff
misconceptions.correction: For a Butterworth design the -3 dB frequency does not depend on the order; only the transition band narrows
misconceptions.evidence: Low-pass at 500 Hz: the -3 dB read-out stays at 500 Hz for N = 1, 4 and 8 while the stopband edge moves from 3872 Hz to 866 Hz

misconceptions.misconception: Coefficients rounded to 16 bits are practically exact, so the filter cannot change much
misconceptions.correction: Sensitivity depends on the structure: high-order direct-form polynomials have very sensitive roots
misconceptions.evidence: 8th-order low-pass at 500 Hz with 16-bit coefficients: the biquad cascade keeps pole radius 0.9279, the direct form becomes unstable with radius 1.0497

misconceptions.misconception: The cutoff of an FIR filter is its -3 dB frequency
misconceptions.correction: For a windowed-sinc design the cutoff is the half-amplitude (-6 dB) point
misconceptions.evidence: FIR low-pass with fc = 500 Hz and M = 32 reports -3 dB at 398 Hz

accessibility.screenReaderScript: Filter design tool with fs = 8000 Hz. Choose a filter type and an IIR or FIR design, then set the frequency, order, Q, comb delay and gain, and coefficient bits. Plots show the magnitude response with the ideal brick-wall response, the phase, group delay, impulse or step response, the pole-zero plot with a stability indicator, and the input and output of a test signal made of 200, 1000 and 3000 Hz tones with a before and after bar chart.

controls.label: Filter type
controls.description: Chooses low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, band-stop, notch, comb or all-pass

controls.label: Design
controls.description: IIR as a cascade of biquads, the same IIR as one direct-form polynomial, or FIR (no feedback; not available for the all-pass)

controls.label: Show
controls.description: Selects the lower plot: phase, group delay, impulse response or step response

controls.label: dB scale
controls.description: Shows the magnitude in dB (-80 to +10 dB) or as a linear gain

controls.label: Cutoff fc / Centre f0
controls.description: Cutoff or centre frequency, mapped logarithmically from 20 to 3500 Hz (slider positions 0-1000)

properties.units: Hz (positions 0-1000 map to 20-3500 Hz; default 623 = 500 Hz)

controls.label: Order N
controls.description: IIR Butterworth order (band-pass and band-stop have order 2N); FIR order M = 8N

controls.label: Q
controls.description: Selectivity of the band-pass, band-stop, notch and all-pass sections

controls.label: Comb delay D
controls.description: Delay of the comb filter in samples

controls.label: Comb gain g
controls.description: Gain of the delayed term of the comb filter

controls.label: Coeff. bits
controls.description: Rounds every coefficient to 4-24 bits; the right end (25) means no rounding (64-bit floating point)

visualElements.description: Magnitude response |H(f)| in dB or linear (maroon), ideal brick-wall response (dashed gray), test-tone markers (gold) and the -3 dB line
Lower plot: unwrapped phase, group delay, impulse response or step response
Pole-zero plot in the z-plane with the unit circle; poles drawn red when on or outside it
Stability status, largest pole radius, order, -3 dB frequencies, passband and stopband or comb and all-pass read-outs
10 ms of the test signal input (gray) and filter output (blue)
Bars with the amplitude of the 200, 1000 and 3000 Hz tones before (gray) and after (maroon) the filter

model.description: Butterworth and RBJ-cookbook biquads from the bilinear transform with prewarping (or Hamming-windowed sinc FIR filters, or comb filters); frequency response, unwrapped phase and analytic group delay on a dense grid; poles and zeros from each section; the test signal is filtered sample by sample with the same, optionally rounded, coefficients.
equations: y[n] = sum_k b_k x[n-k] - sum_{k>=1} a_k y[n-k]
Omega = tan(pi f / fs) (prewarped bilinear transform)
LPF biquad: b = [(1-cos w0)/2, 1-cos w0, (1-cos w0)/2], a = [1+alpha, -2 cos w0, 1-alpha], alpha = sin(w0)/(2Q)
FIR comb: y[n] = x[n] + g x[n-D], |H| = sqrt(1 + g^2 + 2 g cos(w D))
Feedback comb: y[n] = (1-g) x[n] + g y[n-D]
Stable if and only if every pole satisfies |p| < 1
algorithms: Low-pass to band-pass and band-stop transformation
Single-bin DFT over whole cycles for the tone amplitudes
limitations: Only the coefficients are rounded; arithmetic is 64-bit floating point
The phase is undefined at exact zeros of the response and is left blank there
Q is applied to the prewarped analog prototype, so the measured digital bandwidth differs slightly from f0/Q

instructionalStrategies: Compare the same filter as cascade, direct form and FIR
Table of tone amplitudes for each filter family
extensions: Add arithmetic (not only coefficient) quantization to show limit cycles
